title: Best and worst of the road: sleep, hotels, cheap lodging
summary: Gabriel describes bus travel, segregated lodging and how he found cheap rooms and meals while others overspent.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: It seems that way. You seem to have done a lot of road work, you're on the road a lot. I always want to ask people what's the best thing about being on the road and what's the worst thing about traveling and being on the road?

Well the hardest thing is getting your proper sleep which you never get. And most of the time was traveling by bus. And accommodations out on the road back then was bad. Because there were not many hotels up until in the 50s where blacks could stay. But another thing about it, according to what band you was with out there, according to what price you paid in hotels. Now that sounds funny. And also in restaurants. Which I was lucky enough, I had sense enough, not to go in a group for meals or to get a place to stay. And I didn't stay in too many hotels.

I'd always let the band go where they're going. Then I'd go around, hit some of the bars. Look like, see a fella look like he's in the know. Then I'd go up and ask him, where do he eat? He'd say, oh right down there they got the chicken shack or so and so's resting. But I'd say, now where do you eat? Well I eat around there by Miss So and So. You go around there by Miss So and So's little place, you get a better meal and cost you less money. And then while in there I'll say, well, you know anybody that got a room, you know, they want to rent me out for the night or two. Oh Miss Sarah got a spare room over there. Bessie got a spare room over there. I say, good I'll go over there and don't cost me neither the amount of money that the other fella. I remember one trip was down in Fort Wayne, Indiana. I was playing with Deacon Jones Band out of Toledo. I'll say his band, but I'm the fella who got the band together for him. And the fellas went on and rushed to stay at the motel and the hotel. It was costing them something like $90 a week. And I went across the track to a little hotel and I was paying $10 a week. They was paying $4 or $5 a day per meal. And I was eating at Miss Tubbs restaurant for $8 a week.

That's it. Another lady out there in New Iberia, we used to call her Big Sis. When we'd play all through Highway 9, we'd stay in New Iberia. She used to charge us $0.50 a night for rooms. And $0.25 a meal. So I, well, I was quite conservative because I had a family. And I always had to save money to send home. Where most of these fellas out there, they didn't bother with sending any money home. Whether they had a family or not. For instance, they got it. They spent, they looked to borrow for me most of the time. And that happened also when I was working with Jane Mack Shands Band. Fellas couldn't keep a thin quarter in their pocket. Never have over two shirts to wear and do any on one side. Then turn it on the wrong side and wear it again.
